Build the WEB side of the billing bonus track for Switchboard in the ISOLATED COPY /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard-billing, only inside scaffold/web/src (React 19 + Vite + TS, plain CSS with the existing design tokens in src/styles/*.css, inline SVG icons from src/components/icons.tsx; no new dependencies). Never touch /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard, /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/gohlai-assessment, or scaffold/server (another agent is writing the server). Do not run the harness or start servers on ports 4000/5173.

First read: BONUS_BILLING.md and PAYBOX.md (card tokenization in the browser with the PUBLISHABLE key; the card number must NEVER touch our server; test cards; the 3155 card returns requires_action with a next_action.url the browser is sent to), then the current UI in src/ (App.tsx, components/Rail.tsx, Workspace.tsx, InfoPanel.tsx, ReplyBox.tsx, Thread.tsx, api.ts, types.ts, people.ts, styles/*.css) and look at docs/screenshots/05-claim-and-reply.png and 03-inbox.png to match the visual language (dark rail, indigo accent, light surfaces, calm density, system fonts).

SERVER CONTRACT you code against (the server agent is implementing it; admins only, agents get 403 on all of it):
- GET /api/billing?workspace=<id> -> { status: 'none'|'incomplete'|'active'|'past_due'|'canceled', seats: number, canSend: boolean, plainState: string, nextStep: string|null, nextActionUrl: string|null, priceCentsPerSeat: 1200, publishableKey: string, warning?: string }
- POST /api/billing/subscribe {workspace, seats, token} -> 200 { ...same shape as GET } when active; 402 { error: string, nextActionUrl?: string } when the payment did not go through (declined, or bank approval needed: then send the browser to nextActionUrl in the same tab and refresh state when the user returns).
- POST /api/billing/seats {workspace, seats} -> 200 { ...same shape, warning? } | 402 { error }
- POST /api/billing/cancel {workspace} -> 200 { ...same shape }
- For non-canceled states a reply works; for 'canceled' POST /api/conversations/:contact/reply answers 402 {error:'subscription canceled'}.
- Paybox browser tokenization: POST http://localhost:4030/v1/tokens with header Authorization: Bearer <publishableKey from GET /api/billing>, JSON body { card: { number, exp_month, exp_year, cvc } } -> { id: 'tok_...' } (read paybox/server.js to confirm the exact request/response and CORS behaviour; make the base URL a Vite env var VITE_PAYBOX_URL defaulting to http://localhost:4030).

Build:
1. A Billing screen for workspace ADMINS only: reachable from the account menu / rail (a 'Billing' item shown only when my role in the current workspace is admin; use me.workspaces[].role). Agents never see the entry, and if they navigate to it they get a short 'Only admins can manage billing' message.
2. The screen shows, in plain words: the current state sentence (plainState) with a status pill (None -> 'Free trial', Active green, Past due amber, Incomplete amber 'Waiting for payment', Canceled red), seats, monthly cost (seats x $12.00), and 'what to do next' (nextStep) as a clear call to action. Copy must be calm and plain, no jargon.
3. Subscribe form (shown for none/incomplete/canceled): seat count stepper (min 1), live total ('3 seats x $12.00 = $36.00 per month'), card form (number with spacing, expiry MM/YY, CVC; labels, autocomplete attributes cc-number/cc-exp/cc-csc, inline validation messages, Luhn is nice-to-have), a Pay button with loading state that tokenizes in the browser then POSTs only the token to our server. A line stating card details go straight to the payment provider and never to our server. Show a list of the Paybox test cards as a collapsible 'Test cards' hint (this is a demo environment): 4242 4242 4242 4242 succeeds, 4000 0000 0000 0002 declined, 4000 0000 0000 9995 insufficient funds, 4000 0000 0000 0341 first charge ok then declined at renewal, 4000 0025 0000 3155 needs bank approval.
4. Manage section when active/past_due: change seats (stepper + 'Update seats' button, shows the new total, shows the server's warning text e.g. about reducing below current team size, handles 402 with a plain message that the extra charge failed), and a 'Cancel at period end' with a confirm step.
5. States while waiting: incomplete with nextActionUrl -> a banner 'Your bank needs to approve this payment' with a button 'Approve at your bank' that navigates to the URL; poll GET /api/billing every 5 s while status is incomplete or the page was reopened after approval, stop when it changes.
6. Canceled workspace: in the thread, the ReplyBox is disabled with the visible reason 'Sending is paused because the subscription was canceled. An admin can resubscribe in Billing.' (and for admins a link to Billing). The inbox stays readable. Load billing status once per workspace for admins; for non-admins detect canceled from a 402 on reply (toast 'Sending is paused: this workspace's subscription is canceled. Ask an admin.') and disable the box from then on. Past_due: a slim amber notice at the top of the thread area for admins only.
7. Errors as toasts using the existing Toasts mechanism; all controls keyboard reachable, labelled, visible focus; reuse existing button/input classes and tokens; responsive down to 390px.

Keep code plain and human-looking (small components in src/components/billing/*, an src/billing.ts api module and hook, CSS in src/styles/billing.css imported from main.tsx), no emoji, no narration comments. Verify: `cd /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard-billing/scaffold/web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vite build`, then delete dist/. Re-read your own polling/cleanup and 402 handling once for bugs. Final report under 250 words: files, assumptions about the contract, anything unverified.

# Bonus track: billing

Only start this when `npm run check:full` is where you want it. It is scored
separately (10 bonus points) and never makes up for a Must tier that fails.

## The problem

Switchboard is sold per seat, per month. Build that on Paybox (`PAYBOX.md`).

1. A workspace **admin** subscribes the workspace: picks a number of seats,
   enters a card, pays. Agents cannot see or change billing.
2. Card details are entered in your UI and never touch your server.
3. The admin can change the number of seats later.
4. The app always knows the workspace's subscription state, including when it
   changes without anyone clicking anything: a renewal fails, the bank asks
   for approval, Paybox cancels after its retries run out.
5. A workspace whose subscription is **canceled** cannot send messages. It
   can still read its inbox. A workspace that has **never subscribed** is on a
   free trial and can send.
6. The admin sees the current state in plain words and what to do about it.

## Contract additions for the grader

Create the Paybox customer with `metadata.workspace` set to the workspace id.
Accept Paybox webhooks at `POST /webhooks/paybox`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /__grader/billing/subscribe` `{ workspace, seats, token }` | What your UI does when the admin submits the form, with a card token already made. `200` if the subscription is active, `402` if it is not. |
| `POST /__grader/billing/seats` `{ workspace, seats }` | Change the seat count. `200` if changed, `402` if not. |

Add to each workspace in `GET /__grader/snapshot`:

```json
"billing": { "status": "active", "seats": 3, "can_send": true }
```

`status` is `none`, `incomplete`, `active`, `past_due` or `canceled`.
When `can_send` is false, `POST /__grader/reply` for that workspace must
answer `402` and must not send.

## What the grader does

Subscribes a workspace three times in the same instant. Changes seats. Pays
for a second workspace with a card that only works once, then moves the clock
past the renewal and past the retries. Posts a forged webhook. Checks that the
canceled workspace cannot send and the paying one still can. Reads Paybox's
own record of how you called it.

## Left for you to decide (write it in DECISIONS.md)

What a `past_due` workspace is allowed to do, and for how long. What happens
to agents when seats are reduced below the number of people in the workspace.
Whether an admin who removes seats mid-month should be told about the credit.
What the UI shows while a payment is waiting for the bank.
# Paybox — payment provider contract

Base URL `http://localhost:4030`. Only needed for the bonus track.

| Key | Value | Use it from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Publishable | `pk_test_paybox_9a7b3e` | The browser. Can only create card tokens. |
| Secret | `sk_test_paybox_51c0de` | Your server only. Everything else. |
| Webhook signing secret | `whsec_paybox_dev` | Your server only. |

Send keys as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Bodies are JSON. Amounts are in
cents. The one price is `price_seat_monthly`: **1200 per seat per 30 days**.

## Test cards

Any future expiry, any three-digit CVC.

| Number | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `4242 4242 4242 4242` | Always succeeds. |
| `5555 5555 5555 4444` | Always succeeds. |
| `4000 0000 0000 0002` | Every charge is declined (`card_declined`). |
| `4000 0000 0000 9995` | Every charge is declined (`insufficient_funds`). |
| `4000 0000 0000 0341` | First charge succeeds. Every later charge is declined. |
| `4000 0025 0000 3155` | First charge needs the cardholder to approve it at their bank. |
| `4000 0000 0000 0069` | Expired. Rejected when you create the token. |

## The flow

1. **Browser → Paybox:** `POST /v1/tokens` with the publishable key and
   `{ "card": { "number", "exp_month", "exp_year", "cvc" } }`. You get
   `{ "id": "tok_..." }`. A token works once. Paybox counts every card number
   that reaches it through a secret key, because that means the number passed
   through somebody's server.
2. **Server → Paybox:** `POST /v1/customers` `{ name, email, metadata }`.
   Set `metadata.workspace` to the workspace id; it is how Paybox reports
   refer to your customer.
3. `POST /v1/customers/:id/payment_method` `{ token }`.
4. `POST /v1/subscriptions` `{ customer, price, quantity }`.

`POST /v1/subscriptions/:id` `{ quantity }` changes seats.
`POST /v1/subscriptions/:id` `{ cancel_at_period_end: true }` cancels at the
end of the period. `DELETE /v1/subscriptions/:id` cancels now.
`GET /v1/subscriptions/:id`, `GET /v1/subscriptions?customer=`,
`GET /v1/invoices?subscription=`, `GET /v1/customers/:id` read state.

## Things that will catch you out

- **HTTP 200 means Paybox understood you, not that money moved.** Creating a
  subscription with a declining card returns `200` and a subscription whose
  `status` is `incomplete`. Read `status` and `latest_invoice.payment.status`.
- **Subscription status:** `incomplete` (first payment not made yet; expires
  after 23 hours) → `active` → `past_due` (a renewal failed and is being
  retried) → `canceled`. A renewal that fails is retried 3 days and 5 days
  later; after the third failure Paybox cancels the subscription.
- **Authentication.** With the `3155` card the first payment comes back
  `requires_action` with `next_action.url`. Send the user's browser there;
  they approve or decline. You find out the result by webhook, not from that
  page.
- **Seat increases** are charged immediately, pro rata for the rest of the
  period, and are all-or-nothing: if that charge fails you get `402` and the
  seat count does not change. **Seat decreases** take effect immediately and
  the unused amount becomes credit on the next invoice. No refunds.
- **Idempotency-Key** header on `POST`: the same key returns the original
  response and does nothing twice. Without one, a retry creates a second
  customer or a second subscription.

## Webhooks Paybox sends you

`POST http://localhost:4000/webhooks/paybox`, signed exactly like Pigeon:
`x-paybox-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">`.

```json
{ "id": "evt_...", "type": "invoice.payment_failed", "created": 1795000000,
  "data": { "object": { "...": "the subscription or invoice as it was when the event was created" } } }
```

Types: `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`,
`customer.subscription.deleted`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`,
`invoice.payment_action_required`.

Delivery is at least once and in no particular order. `invoice.paid` can
arrive before `customer.subscription.created`. The object inside an event is a
photograph of the past; `GET /v1/subscriptions/:id` is the present.
The URL is public: anyone can post a fake "payment succeeded" to it.

## The test clock

Nothing renews while you wait, so move time yourself:

```
curl -X POST localhost:4030/v1/test_clock/advance -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"days": 31}'
curl localhost:4030/v1/test_clock
```

Advancing runs every renewal, retry and expiry that falls due, in order, and

- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task.
